display_title: Artificial Intelligence Hybrid Survival Assessment System for Robot-Assisted Proctectomy: A Retrospective Cohort Study
summary: RAP-AIscore is an interpretable postoperative overall-survival model developed in a retrospective two-center study of 506 patients undergoing robot-assisted proctectomy, with internal validation and independent retrospective SYEMH evaluation.
research_question: Can a systematically selected hybrid survival-machine-learning framework provide interpretable and externally validated postoperative overall-survival risk stratification for patients with rectal cancer undergoing robot-assisted proctectomy?
author_summary: This retrospective two-center study evaluated 506 unique patients undergoing robot-assisted proctectomy for rectal cancer. The NSCVRCS Meta cohort included 384 patients divided into development and internal-validation subsets; an independent SYEMH cohort included 122 patients. A comparison of 132 candidate survival-modeling schemes selected Surv.coxboost + Surv.aorsf and yielded an interpretable model with 10 predictors. RAP-AIscore showed internal time-dependent survival discrimination and separated patients into three prognostic states. Independent SYEMH evaluation was retrospective: its 1-year AUC was 0.587, with 2- and 3-year AUCs of 0.754 and 0.810. Prospective clinical utility and improved survival from model-guided care remain unestablished.

qa.question: What population was RAP-AIscore developed for?
qa.answer: Patients with rectal cancer undergoing robot-assisted proctectomy; the study modeled postoperative overall survival retrospectively.

qa.question: How many independent patients and cohorts were studied?
qa.answer: There were 506 unique patients: 384 in NSCVRCS Meta and 122 in independent SYEMH. NSCVRCS Discovery n=268 and Replication n=116 are subsets of Meta, not additional patients.

qa.question: How were 132 modeling schemes compared?
qa.answer: The study systematically compared candidate survival-modeling schemes and selected Surv.coxboost + Surv.aorsf, which achieved the highest average C-index, 0.833.

qa.question: What performance was observed internally?
qa.answer: At 12/36/60/72 months, AUCs were 0.851/0.849/0.902/0.915 in Replication, 0.911/0.924/0.931/0.948 in Meta, and 0.927/0.960/0.949/0.962 in Discovery. These are retrospective time-dependent discrimination results.

qa.question: What happened in independent SYEMH validation?
qa.answer: In the independent retrospective cohort, 1-/2-/3-year AUCs were 0.587/0.754/0.810. Early discrimination was modest. High-versus-low survival differed at P < 0.0001 and three-state discrimination at P < 0.001.

qa.question: Does RAP-AIscore have proven prospective clinical benefit?
qa.answer: No. The retrospective model-development, internal-validation and external-evaluation findings do not establish prospective clinical utility or survival benefit from model-guided care.

limitations: The two-center study and independent external evaluation were retrospective.
Prospective clinical utility and survival benefit from model-guided management were not established.
External 1-year discrimination was modest, with AUC 0.587.
Generalizability to all hospitals and RAP populations was not established.

The Results text reports Replication low/intermediate/high counts of 68/20/19, which sum to 107 and do not reconcile with the stated Replication cohort size of 116. These subgroup counts are retained as article-reported values; the denominator discrepancy is unresolved and must not be interpreted as documented exclusions or a complete partition of all 116 patients.

related_papers.relationship: Related hybrid survival-machine-learning framework developed by the same research program in a different clinical population; AIHFLevel addresses advanced heart failure with renal dysfunction, whereas RAP-AIscore addresses postoperative survival after robot-assisted proctectomy. The models do not validate one another.
